name: Ross Stores
fiscalYearEnd: Saturday nearest January 31 (fiscal 2025 ended 2026-01-31; fiscal 2024 ended 2025-02-01)
description: Ross Stores runs off-price apparel and home-fashion stores under two banners, Ross Dress for Less (1,904 stores) and the lower-priced dd's DISCOUNTS (363 stores), all in the US plus Guam and Puerto Rico. It buys brand-name overstock, past-season and in-season goods from manufacturers and other retailers late in the buying cycle, then sells at 20 to 70 percent below department-store prices. Money is the gap between that cheap buying and its shelf prices (operating margin 11.9 percent in fiscal 2025) on very high inventory turnover; it reports one segment. About 85 percent of staff work in stores.

businessLines.name: Ross Dress for Less
businessLines.how: Customers pay at the register for brand-name goods that Ross bought cheaply (opportunistic, late-season, packaway buys); revenue is volume through 1,900 stores with new stores the main growth lever, margin depends on buying price versus shelf price.
businessLines.description: Off-price apparel, accessories, footwear and home fashions for the whole family, priced 20% to 60% below department and specialty store regular prices

businessLines.name: dd's DISCOUNTS
businessLines.how: Same off-price buying model aimed at value-driven customers at a more moderate price point than the Ross banner.
businessLines.description: More moderately priced first-quality in-season apparel, accessories, footwear and home fashions, priced 20% to 70% below moderate department and discount store prices

whatsNext.text: Store expansion: plan raised to about 115 new stores in fiscal 2026 (47 opened in Q2); 51 planned for the quarter ending 2026-10-31 (41 Ross, 10 dd's)
